title: Reconnect to existing sessions instead of creating new upon unclean websocket close.
body:
### Checklist

- [X] I have searched the [existing issues](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues) for similar issues.
- [X] I added a very descriptive title to this issue.
- [X] I have provided sufficient information below to help reproduce this issue.

### Summary

Similar to the issues linked, if the network connection is intermittent/flaky the existing session is lost and a new one created, causing unpleasant/unexpected user experience.

See:

https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues/1386
https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues/1628
https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues/6442

### Reproducible Code Example

```Python
import streamlit as st
import time

if "counter" not in st.session_state:
    st.session_state.counter = 0

st.write(f"Run count = {st.session_state.counter}")

st.session_state.counter += 1

time.sleep(3)

st.rerun()
```


### Steps To Reproduce

1. Run the reproducible code example provided in streamlit on one server host.
2. Observe the "Run count = X" increase steadily in a client host different from the server host.
3. Disable the client network connection and wait for some arbitrary time duration.
4. Re-enable the client network connection.
5. Observer the "Run count = X" start from zero again.

### Expected Behavior

The user session should be restored so they may continue where they left off in the face of their network/internet connection being flaky (packet drops, high latency etc) causing unclean websocket close behind the scenes.

### Current Behavior

Observe streamlit warning log "Session with id %s is already connected! Connecting to a new session." and user loses their streamlit session and starts afresh.

### Is this a regression?

- [ ] Yes, this used to work in a previous version.

### Debug info

- Streamlit version: 1.35
- Python version: 3.10
- Operating System: Windows 11
- Browser: Chrome/Firefox


### Additional Information

I have been able to make a potentially naive code change (will link a PR as a proposal to this issue) which I am unable to run against full test suite because I have been unable to build the streamlit project. I have been able to test partially by modifying the python code in my installed streamlit venv.

This issue reports that when a WebSocket connection closes uncleanly (e.g., due to network disruptions), Streamlit creates a new session instead of reconnecting to the existing one, causing users to lose their session state.

**Root cause analysis:** The issue originates in `lib/streamlit/runtime/websocket_session_manager.py` in the `connect_session()` method. When a client attempts to reconnect with an existing session ID, the code checks if that session is already in `_active_session_info_by_id` (line 103). If it is, a warning is logged ("Session with id %s is already connected!") and a **new** session is created instead. The session can only be restored from storage if it's NOT currently active.

The core problem is a race condition: on an unclean WebSocket close, the server may not have detected the disconnect yet, so the session remains "active" in memory. When the client quickly reconnects with the same session ID, the server sees it as "already connected" and creates a new session instead of allowing reconnection. A potential fix would need to handle this case by either closing the existing connection first, implementing a grace period, or using a different strategy for tracking active vs. disconnected sessions.

### Related Issues

1. **[#9031](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues/9031)** - "Current recommended way to deal with restarted Streamlit sessions" - Directly related issue where users request better session recovery mechanisms after unexpected restarts.

2. **[#11012](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues/11012)** - "Preserve session state (e.g. in file, database, or localstorage)" - Related enhancement request for persisting session state across browser sessions, which would help mitigate the impact of session loss.

3. **[#12108](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues/12108)** - "Frequent websocket connection drops on higher ping_interval" - Related WebSocket stability issue that can trigger the reconnection problem described in this issue.
